name: Adyen N.V.
price_source: StockAnalysis.com (AMS:ADYEN) statistics page; cross-checked vs Yahoo Finance (prev close EUR 875.80 on 2026-06-19)
structural_change: No genuine deterioration — classic fear/growth-to-value rotation. FY2025 net revenue +18% reported / +21% cc to EUR 2,364M, EBITDA +26% to EUR 1,246M with margin expanding to 53% (55% in H2), FCF conversion 87%, robust net cash ~EUR 10.6B, FY2026 guidance net revenue +20-22% cc with EBITDA margin held ~53% and a path to >55% by 2028. Stock is -43% off 52w high and -69% off the 2021 ATH purely on multiple compression (fwd P/E from ~100x in 2021 to ~22.6x today). Only real structural watch-item: SBC rising modestly with US expansion and intensifying competition (Stripe, big-tech, in-house processing), but margins are still expanding — quality intact.
owner_fcf_base: Owner FCF base = FY2025 reported FCF ~EUR 907M minus 100% SBC (~2% of EUR 2,364M revenue = ~EUR 47M) = ~EUR 860M. Per diluted share ~EUR 27.2. Adyen runs structurally low SBC (~1-2% of revenue) due to the Netherlands 20% variable-pay cap, so the owner-earnings haircut is small versus typical US tech.

conservador.note: Phase 1 (yr1-5) owner-FCF CAGR 14% (deceleration vs ~20% guide on share-loss/pricing pressure), Phase 2 (yr6-10) declining 14%->6%, terminal g 2.5%, WACC 9.3%. Reasonable-pessimistic, not apocalyptic: still a healthy compounder, just margin/growth normalization.

base.note: Phase 1 19% CAGR (in line with 20-22% FY2026 cc guidance, slight fade), Phase 2 declining 19%->7%, terminal g 3.0%, WACC 9.3%. Reflects continued high-margin reinvestment, operating leverage toward >55% EBITDA margin by 2028.

optimista.note: Phase 1 23% CAGR (unified-commerce + platforms/embedded finance share gains, US scaling), Phase 2 declining 23%->8%, terminal g 3.5%, WACC 9.3%. Adyen extends single-platform moat and wallet share.

multiple_rationale: 5y average forward P/E (~45x) is inflated by the 2021-2022 bubble when Adyen traded ~80-100x; that is not a clean normalized anchor. Apply a deliberate haircut to ~32x fair forward P/E. Justification: a ~20% grower with 50%+ EBITDA margins, asset-light single-platform model, high ROIC reinvestment runway and ~EUR 10.6B net cash easily supports a low-30s multiple (implied PEG ~1.5, well below the absurd 2021 levels). The haircut is for multiple-regime normalization (rates higher, competition from Stripe/big-tech), NOT for fundamental deterioration. iv_multiple = FY2026 EPS est EUR 40.67 (FY2025 diluted EPS EUR 33.61 x ~1.21 growth) x 32 = ~EUR 1,301/sh.
sanity_notes: Mcap sanity: 874.20 EUR x 0.0316B sh = EUR 27.6B -> x EUR/USD 1.146 = ~USD 31.6B, matching the known ~EUR 28B / ~USD 32B scale (StockAnalysis EUR 27.58B). Shares ~31.55M outstanding / ~32M diluted confirmed across StockAnalysis + Yahoo — no millions/billions or currency confusion. Magnitude check: all IVs (EUR 1,165-1,903) sit within the 30%-300% band of price (EUR 262-2,623), so no units/share/FX error. Both methods agree directionally well above the EUR 874 price: DCF-weighted EUR 1,435 and multiple anchor EUR 1,301 bracket a reconciled IV of ~EUR 1,362 (~56% upside). Weights 0.45 DCF / 0.55 multiple: Adyen is a proven, profitable, net-cash compounder (lean toward multiple anchor), but still a high-growth name with real competitive/de-rating uncertainty and DCF that can over-credit decades of high-ROIC reinvestment, so not the full 0.35/0.65 stable-compounder split. DCF runs hot here mainly because of the large net cash add-back and low capital intensity. Key risks to the thesis: competitive share loss (Stripe, in-house processing by large merchants), take-rate compression, and FX (EUR strength dampening reported USD-denominated volume). All figures in EUR, the quotation currency.
